messages:
lina: Hey team — our rerank calls are coming back with weird negative numbers and some clearly better candidates are getting lower scores. We used the Console's "Copy cURL" example and then pasted to our CI job.
noah: Sorry about that, can you paste the exact cURL payload you copied from Console (redact token)?
lina: Yep, here's what Console gave me when I hit Copy -> cURL:
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"top travel backpacks","candidates":"[\"lightweight daypack\",\"waterproof hiking pack\",\"urban commuter bag\",\"expedition pack\"]","top_k":3}'
```
lina: I tried swapping to an actual array and it stopped throwing 400s, but scores still odd: server returned [ -0.12, 0.92, 0.05, 0.33 ] which makes no sense for that list.
sam: Thanks for the sample. Two likely issues: 1) the console copy flow is emitting the candidates as a JSON-encoded string (so the service sees one big string instead of N candidates). That changes tokenization and scoring. 2) There's a recently-introduced default for `score_normalization` in rerank v1.0 that affects scaling; mixing types + normalization can surface as negative or unexpected magnitudes.
noah: Could you confirm whether you sent candidates as plain strings (e.g., ["a","b"]) or as objects (e.g., [{"id":"1","text":"a"}, ...])? Also which model: hosted/dedicated and model id?
lina: Hosted, model `rerank-open-1.0`. I sent plain strings after switching, still odd. I didn't include any `score_normalization` field.
sam: Ok. If the Console payload had `candidates` serialized as a string, the backend will attempt to treat it as one candidate; depending on tokenization it can produce tiny or negative logits after internal transforms. We should give a concrete repro. Can you run this exact payload (works via here-doc) and paste the response?
noah: For others reading: common gotcha is shell quoting. The Console "Copy cURL" flow tried to make it shell-safe but ended up double-encoding the array. Short-term workaround: write payload to a file or use a bash here-doc with single-quote delimiter so the shell doesn't interpret backslashes. Example:
```
cat > rr_payload.json <<'JSON'
{"query":"top travel backpacks","candidates":["lightweight daypack","waterproof hiking pack","urban commuter bag","expedition pack"],"top_k":3}
JSON
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @rr_payload.json
```
lina: Using the here-doc fixed my scores — now getting [0.08, 0.88, 0.22, 0.35]. Much closer to expected.
tara: Thanks for flagging. I found the console generator PR that changed the cURL template — it JSON.stringified arrays for copy safety, which was a regression. I'll revert the generator and update docs. Also adding a short "Rerank: payload gotchas" note in the API doc.
sam: On runtime side we'll also add stricter validation: if `candidates` is type string and looks like a JSON array (starts with '[' and contains quotes/commas), return 422 with message: "candidates must be an array or array of objects; you may be copying a stringified JSON array from the Console. Use an array or objects." This should avoid silent mis-scoring.
noah: Filing internal ticket RERANK-451 for console revert + docs update + validation. Lina, we'll link that to this thread and escalate.
support-bot: status set to escalated  linked RERANK-451
lina: Appreciate the quick triage. One more question: should we include `score_normalization: true` to avoid negative-ish numbers?
sam: Normalization affects scale and comparability across queries. We default to enabled in newer models, but if you see negatives it's usually the parsing issue. If you want deterministic behavior include `score_normalization: true` explicitly. We'll add a docs snippet showing normalized vs raw outputs.
noah: We'll keep the thread open until console patch + docs PR are live. tagging @tara and @sam for follow-ups.
tara: I'll push docs PR with examples (curl here-doc + JS fetch) and call out the 512 candidate limit and tokenization note.
support-bot: follow-up task created: RERANK-451 assigned to sam,tara ; status: in_progress
lina: Works for us — thanks everyone :heart:
